def: The function and the set of practices that manage employees moving to work in another country.

formal.ex: The Group's [[international mobility]] programme applies to all employees assigned outside their home country for more than three months.

everyday.ex: I'll loop in [[global mobility]] - they'll know whether she needs a visa.

note_fr: Dans les groupes anglo-saxons, « Global Mobility » désigne souvent l'équipe elle-même (« ask Global Mobility »), comme on dirait « la mobilité internationale » en interne. « Mobility » seul peut aussi viser la mobilité interne : précisez « international » ou « global » s'il y a un doute.

fr: salarié en mobilité internationale (expatrié ou détaché)
def: An employee who has been sent by the company to work in another country for a defined period.

formal.ex: Each [[international assignee]] shall receive a written assignment letter before departure.

everyday.ex: We've got twelve [[assignees]] in France at the moment, mostly engineers from the Pune office.

informal.ex: Most of the [[expats]] live in the same part of town and send their kids to the international school.

note_fr: « Assignee » couvre aussi bien le détaché que l'expatrié : l'anglais ne fait pas la distinction juridique française, il faut l'ajouter. Accent sur la dernière syllabe. « Expat » est familier mais très courant, y compris par écrit dans un e-mail interne.

def: A worker sent by their employer to carry out work in another EU country for a limited period, while remaining employed by that employer.

formal.ex: A [[posted worker]] remains employed by the sending undertaking throughout the period of posting.

everyday.ex: He's [[been posted to]] our Lyon site for six months to set up the new line.

note_fr: « Posted worker » est le terme du droit européen, à préférer à « detached worker » (calque) ou « seconded worker » (plus britannique et plus large). Aux États-Unis, la notion n'existe pas : expliquez qu'il s'agit d'un régime européen qui impose une partie des règles du pays d'accueil.

def: The company in the destination country where an internationally mobile employee actually works.

formal.ex: The [[host entity]] shall bear the costs of the assignment unless otherwise agreed between the entities concerned.

everyday.ex: Who's paying for her flat - us or the [[host company]]?

collocations: to recharge costs to the host entity
note_fr: On oppose « host » (accueil) à « home » (origine) : « home entity / host entity », « home country / host country ». Ne traduisez pas par « welcoming company ». Pour un salarié détaché, l'entité d'accueil n'est pas l'employeur juridique : précisez-le dans les échanges avec le siège.

def: The company that employs the mobile employee before the move and, in many cases, during it.

formal.ex: The Assignee shall remain employed by the [[home entity]] for the duration of the assignment.

everyday.ex: She's still on the [[home company]]'s payroll, so her French contract carries on.

collocations: to remain employed by the home entity
to return to the home entity
note_fr: « Home » ici ne veut pas dire « domicile » mais « d'origine ». Attention : la société d'origine n'est pas toujours la société mère ; dans un groupe américain, l'entité d'origine peut être la filiale française.

def: An employee recruited directly in the country where they work, on local terms, with no expatriate benefits.

formal.ex: A [[locally hired employee]] is not eligible for the allowances set out in this Policy.

everyday.ex: He's British, but he's a [[local hire]] - we took him on in Paris on a standard French contract.

collocations: to convert an assignee to a local hire
note_fr: La nationalité ne compte pas : un Britannique recruté à Paris sur un CDI français est un « local hire ». C'est l'employeur et le contrat qui font le statut, pas le passeport.

def: A permanent move of an employee to a group company in another country, usually with a new local contract.

formal.ex: A [[permanent international transfer]] entails the termination of the home employment contract and the conclusion of a new contract with the receiving entity.

everyday.ex: It's not an assignment, it's an [[international transfer]] - she's moving to Chicago for good.

informal.ex: He's [[moving over]] to the London office in January and won't be coming back.

note_fr: La mutation définitive (« one-way move ») s'oppose à la mission (« assignment ») qui prévoit un retour. En droit français, mettre fin au contrat d'origine pour en conclure un autre à l'étranger doit être organisé avec soin (rupture ou suspension, reprise d'ancienneté) : faites-le préciser par écrit.

def: The document that sets out the terms of an international assignment: destination, duration, pay, allowances and return.

formal.ex: The terms of the assignment are set out in the [[letter of assignment]], which forms an addendum to the employment contract.

everyday.ex: Has she signed her [[assignment letter]] yet? We can't book the movers until she has.

collocations: the terms of the assignment letter
note_fr: En France, la lettre de mission prend souvent la forme d'un avenant au contrat de travail : elle modifie des éléments essentiels (lieu, rémunération) et suppose donc l'accord écrit du salarié. Ne confondez pas avec « letter of appointment » (lettre d'engagement).

def: The group document that defines the categories of international moves and the support and benefits attached to each.

formal.ex: Allowances are calculated in accordance with the Group's [[international assignment policy]] in force at the start date.

everyday.ex: The [[mobility policy]] only covers school fees up to the age of eighteen.

note_fr: « Policy » ici = politique interne, pas « police ». En France, une politique groupe n'est pas un document contractuel : ce qui engage vis-à-vis du salarié, c'est la lettre de mission ou l'avenant signé.

def: An international assignment that typically lasts between one and five years, often with the family moving too.

formal.ex: A [[long-term assignment]] is defined as an assignment of more than twelve months, during which the Assignee relocates to the host country.

everyday.ex: It's a three-year [[long-term assignment]], so the whole family's going out.

collocations: to go on a long-term assignment
note_fr: La durée-seuil varie selon les groupes (souvent plus de douze mois) : vérifiez la politique, ce n'est pas une notion légale. Ne dites pas « long-duration mission » : « mission » évoque en anglais une mission diplomatique, religieuse ou militaire.

def: An assignment abroad of a few months, usually without the family relocating.

formal.ex: Employees on a [[short-term assignment]] shall be provided with serviced accommodation and a daily allowance.

everyday.ex: Can we do it as a six-month [[short-term assignment]] instead of a full move?

informal.ex: She did a six-month [[stint]] in Singapore last year.

note_fr: Une mission courte n'échappe pas pour autant aux règles : déclaration de détachement, A1, fiscalité et immigration s'appliquent dès le premier jour selon les pays. « Stint » est familier mais très naturel à l'oral.

def: An employee who makes trips abroad for work without being assigned or relocated there.

formal.ex: Frequent [[business travellers]] must record the number of days spent in each country.
formal.ex_us: Frequent [[business travelers]] must record the number of days spent in each country.

everyday.ex: He doesn't live there - he just [[travels for work]] two weeks a month.

informal.ex: Our sales director is a real [[road warrior]] - she's in a different country every week.

note_fr: Orthographe : « traveller » (UK, deux l) / « traveler » (US, un l). Les déplacements fréquents peuvent, à partir d'un certain nombre de jours, créer des obligations fiscales, sociales ou de détachement : d'où le suivi des jours (« day counting »).

fr: indemnité de coût de la vie
def: An allowance that compensates an assignee for higher prices of everyday goods and services in the host location.

formal.ex: A [[cost-of-living allowance]] shall be paid where the host location index exceeds that of the home location.

everyday.ex: Zurich's so expensive that her [[COLA]] is almost a third of her base salary.

note_fr: COLA se prononce /ˈkəʊlə/ comme la boisson. Aux États-Unis, « COLA » désigne aussi la revalorisation annuelle des salaires ou des pensions selon l'inflation (« cost-of-living adjustment ») : précisez « allowance » dans un contexte de mobilité.

def: An extra payment for working in a location with difficult living conditions, such as poor security, climate or healthcare.

formal.ex: A [[hardship allowance]] is payable for locations classified as difficult by the Group's external provider.
formal.ex_us: A [[hardship premium]] is payable for locations classified as difficult by the Group's external provider.

everyday.ex: Lagos still qualifies for [[hardship pay]], but Johannesburg doesn't any more.

collocations: to qualify for a hardship allowance
note_fr: « Hardship » = conditions de vie pénibles, pas difficulté financière personnelle. Ne confondez pas avec la prime de pénibilité française (travaux pénibles) : ici c'est le lieu qui est difficile, pas le poste.

fr: indemnité de logement / prise en charge du logement
def: A payment, or a capped budget, to cover the assignee's rent in the host location.

formal.ex: The [[housing allowance]] shall be capped at the amount determined for the assignee's family size and host location.

everyday.ex: Her [[housing budget]] won't stretch to a three-bedroom flat in central London.
everyday.ex_us: Her [[housing budget]] won't stretch to a three-bedroom apartment in central London.

note_fr: « Flat » (UK) / « apartment » (US). Un avantage logement pris en charge par l'employeur est en principe un élément de rémunération imposable et soumis à cotisations : vérifiez le traitement dans chaque pays.

fr: congé dans le pays d'origine (voyage annuel)
def: Paid trips back to the home country for the assignee and family, usually once a year, under the mobility policy.

formal.ex: The Assignee and accompanying family members shall be entitled to one [[home leave]] trip per assignment year in economy class.

everyday.ex: We're using our [[home leave]] to go back to Bordeaux for Christmas.

informal.ex: The company pays for one [[trip home]] a year - anything else is on us.

collocations: to combine home leave with business
note_fr: Le « home leave » est un avantage de la politique de mobilité (prise en charge du voyage), pas un congé supplémentaire : les jours pris restent des congés payés, sauf disposition contraire. Ne le confondez pas avec « leave at home ».

fr: frais de scolarité (prise en charge pour les enfants)
def: The cost of educating the assignee's children in the host location, often paid by the employer up to a cap.

formal.ex: An [[education allowance]] covering tuition at an international or bilingual school shall be granted for each eligible child.

everyday.ex: The [[school fees]] at the American School are eye-watering, so we capped them.
everyday.ex_us: The [[school tuition]] at the American School is crazy expensive, so we capped it.

note_fr: « Fees » (UK) / « tuition » (US) : un Américain parle de « tuition » même pour une école primaire privée. En anglais britannique, « tuition » désigne plutôt l'enseignement lui-même (« private tuition » = cours particuliers).

def: The spouse or partner and children who move abroad with the assignee.

formal.ex: Allowances shall be determined by reference to the number of [[accompanying family members]] residing in the host country.

everyday.ex: Is he going out on his own, or is the [[family]] coming too?

note_fr: « Accompanied / unaccompanied assignment » : mission avec ou sans famille. Le statut a des effets sur le logement, l'école et les titres de séjour : vérifiez-le dès le début du projet.

def: The return of an assignee and family to the home country at the end of an assignment, and the support provided for it.

formal.ex: On completion of the assignment, the Company shall bear the cost of [[repatriation]] to the home country.

everyday.ex: She's [[coming back]] to Paris in June, and we still haven't found her a role.

note_fr: Prononciation différente : UK /ˌriːpætri-/, US /ˌriːpeɪtri-/. En anglais, « repatriation » sert aussi pour les fonds ou une dépouille : en RH, le contexte suffit. Le verbe « to repatriate » est surtout écrit ; à l'oral on dit « to come back », « to bring someone back ».

def: The main office of a group, where central management and group functions are based.

formal.ex: Any departure from this policy requires the prior written approval of [[head office]].
formal.ex_us: Any departure from this policy requires the prior written approval of [[headquarters]].

everyday.ex: We'll need to run it past [[head office]] before we promise anything.
everyday.ex_us: We'll need to run it past [[corporate]] before we promise anything.

informal.ex: [[HQ]] want the new appraisal form live everywhere by March.

collocations: to run something past head office
note_fr: « Headquarters » est pluriel en forme mais s'accorde au singulier ou au pluriel. Les Américains disent volontiers « corporate » (« corporate wants... ») pour le siège. En anglais britannique, un nom collectif comme « HQ » prend souvent un verbe au pluriel.

def: The company that owns or controls one or more subsidiaries.

formal.ex: The French subsidiary is wholly owned by the [[parent company]], incorporated in Delaware.

everyday.ex: The [[parent]] wants every subsidiary on the same HR system by next year.

note_fr: Ne dites pas « mother company » (calque). Rappel utile au siège : la société mère n'est pas l'employeur des salariés de la filiale française, sauf situation exceptionnelle de co-emploi.

def: A rule or set of rules defined by head office to apply in every country where the group operates.

formal.ex: This [[group-wide policy]] applies to all entities, subject to mandatory provisions of local law.
formal.ex_us: This [[company-wide policy]] applies to all entities, subject to mandatory provisions of local law.

everyday.ex: The new [[global policy]] on gifts went out yesterday, and nobody in Paris was consulted.

collocations: to roll out a global policy
note_fr: Une politique groupe ne s'impose en France qu'en respectant le droit local et les procédures : selon son contenu, elle peut devoir être intégrée au règlement intérieur ou faire l'objet d'une information-consultation du CSE. Pensez-y avant de dire « yes, we'll implement it ».

fr: droit local (le droit du pays concerné)
def: The law of the country in which an entity operates or an employee works.

formal.ex: Where this policy conflicts with [[applicable local law]], the latter shall prevail.

everyday.ex: That works in Texas, but [[local law]] won't let us do it here.

note_fr: « Local » ne veut pas dire « municipal » ici : pour un siège étranger, « local law » = le droit français. Formule réflexe à placer dans toute politique groupe : « subject to local law » ou « to the extent permitted by local law ».

def: The number of hours between the local time in two places.

formal.ex: Owing to the [[time difference]], the call has been scheduled at 4 p.m. Paris time.

everyday.ex: With a nine-hour [[time difference]], there's no slot that works for everyone in California and Bangalore.

note_fr: « Jet lag » est la fatigue du voyage, pas le décalage horaire entre deux villes. Précisez toujours le fuseau dans une invitation (« 9 a.m. ET / 3 p.m. CET »). L'Inde a un décalage d'une demi-heure par rapport à l'Europe : vérifiez avant d'envoyer.

def: A meeting by phone or video that brings together participants from several countries.

formal.ex: The quarterly [[global teleconference]] of HR Directors will be held on Tuesday 14 March.

everyday.ex: I'm on the [[global call]] till eight tonight, so let's catch up tomorrow.

note_fr: « Conference » seul désigne plutôt un congrès ; dites « call », « conference call » ou « video call ». « To dial in » s'emploie encore même quand on clique sur un lien. Attention à « eventually » (= finalement) et « actually » (= en fait) : deux faux amis fréquents en réunion.

def: A visa that allows a foreign national to enter and live in a country for more than three months.

formal.ex: The employee must obtain a [[long-stay visa]] from the French consulate before travelling to France.

everyday.ex: Her [[visa]] still hasn't come through, so we've pushed the start date back.

collocations: to apply for a long-stay visa
a visa equivalent to a residence permit
note_fr: Le visa permet d'entrer ; le titre de séjour (« residence permit ») permet de rester ; l'autorisation de travail (« work authorisation ») permet de travailler. Un siège étranger confond souvent les trois : séparez-les clairement.

def: The language normally used for communication inside a company or group.

formal.ex: English is the [[working language]] of the Group; however, documents provided to employees in France shall also be made available in French.

everyday.ex: English may be the [[company language]], but the handbook still has to be in French here.

note_fr: Point clé pour un siège anglophone : en France, les documents qui fixent des obligations au salarié ou dont il a besoin pour travailler doivent en principe être rédigés en français (avec des exceptions, notamment pour les documents venant de l'étranger). Un plan de bonus en anglais seul peut être contesté.

fr: s'installer à l'étranger / être muté (avec déménagement)
def: To move to live and work in a different place, usually because the employer asks or offers it.

formal.ex: Employees who agree [[to relocate]] shall receive the support described in Section 4.

everyday.ex: Would you be up for [[moving]] to Dublin for a couple of years?

informal.ex: They [[upped sticks]] and moved the whole family to Singapore.
informal.ex_us: They [[pulled up stakes]] and moved the whole family to Singapore.

note_fr: Accent : UK /ˌriːləʊˈkeɪt/ (sur « -cate »), US souvent /ˈriːloʊkeɪt/ (sur la première syllabe). « To up sticks » est britannique, « to pull up stakes » américain.

def: To carry out one's job remotely while physically staying in another country.

formal.uk: to work remotely from another country
formal.us: to work remotely from another country
formal.ex: Employees wishing [[to work remotely from another country]] must obtain prior approval from HR.

everyday.ex: Can I [[work from abroad]] for a month while my mother's in hospital in Lisbon?

collocations: a temporary remote work abroad request
note_fr: « Abroad » est un adverbe : on dit « to work abroad », jamais « to work in abroad » ni « to go to abroad ». Même quelques semaines à l'étranger peuvent avoir des effets fiscaux, sociaux et en matière d'immigration : d'où une procédure d'accord préalable.

def: The central HR function at head office, which sets policies for the whole group.

formal.ex: Requests for exceptions shall be submitted to [[Group Human Resources]] for approval.
formal.ex_us: Requests for exceptions shall be submitted to [[Corporate Human Resources]] for approval.

everyday.ex: [[Group HR]] are asking for our headcount figures by Friday.
everyday.ex_us: [[Corporate HR]] is asking for our headcount figures by Friday.

note_fr: Les groupes britanniques disent « Group HR » ; les groupes américains « corporate HR » ou « global HR ». Accord au pluriel fréquent en anglais britannique (« Group HR are... »), au singulier en américain.

def: A company that exists in law and can sign contracts and employ people in its own name.

formal.ex: Each employee shall be employed by a single [[legal entity]] within the Group.

everyday.ex: Which [[entity]] is she actually employed by - the French one or the Irish one?

note_fr: Les groupes raisonnent par « business lines » ; le droit du travail raisonne par entité juridique. Rappelez-le au siège : c'est l'entité qui signe le contrat, déclare les salaires et répond devant les prud'hommes.

def: Differences in values, habits and ways of communicating between people from different countries.

formal.ex: Managers should be made aware of [[cultural differences]] in the way feedback is given and received.

everyday.ex: It's partly [[a cultural thing]] - in France people argue in meetings, and it's not personal.

collocations: to bear in mind cultural differences
note_fr: « Culture » s'emploie au singulier pour une organisation (« our culture ») ; on parle des différences au pluriel. « It's a cultural thing » est très naturel à l'oral pour désamorcer un malentendu.

def: The country where a person is considered resident for income tax purposes.

formal.ex: The Assignee's [[tax residence]] shall be determined in accordance with domestic law and any applicable tax treaty.
formal.ex_us: The Assignee's [[tax residency]] shall be determined in accordance with domestic law and any applicable tax treaty.

everyday.ex: Once he's spent more than half the year here, he'll probably [[be tax resident]] in France.

note_fr: « Residence » (UK) / « residency » (US, plus courant). La résidence fiscale ne dépend pas que du nombre de jours : en France, le foyer, l'activité professionnelle et le centre des intérêts économiques comptent aussi. Ne promettez rien sans conseil fiscal.

def: The price of one currency in terms of another.

formal.ex: Allowances shall be converted at the [[exchange rate]] applicable on the first business day of each month.

everyday.ex: With the [[exchange rate]] where it is, his dollar salary's worth a lot less in euros.

note_fr: « Change » seul ne veut pas dire « devises » : on parle de « currency » (la monnaie) et de « foreign exchange » ou « FX ». Dans une lettre de mission, précisez toujours la monnaie de paiement et la date de conversion.

def: A short trip to the host location before the assignment so that the employee, and often the partner, can see housing, schools and the office.

formal.ex: The Company shall bear the cost of one [[pre-assignment visit]] of up to five days for the assignee and partner.

everyday.ex: They're going over on a [[look-see trip]] next week before they decide.

collocations: to go on a look-see trip
note_fr: « Look-see » est familier mais c'est le terme du métier, y compris dans les politiques. Ne traduisez pas par « reconnaissance trip », qui évoque un repérage militaire.

def: The online notice a foreign employer must file with the French labour authorities before posting a worker to France.

formal.ex: The foreign employer shall submit a [[prior declaration of posting]] to the labour inspectorate before the work begins.

everyday.ex: Has anyone filed the [[posting declaration]] for the two engineers arriving from Pune on Monday?

collocations: to keep a copy on site
note_fr: Côté français, c'est l'employeur étranger qui déclare, avant le début de la prestation, via la plateforme en ligne SIPSI ; l'entreprise d'accueil doit vérifier que c'est fait, sous peine de sanctions. Dites « file » ou « submit » une déclaration, pas « make a declaration », qui sonne comme une déclaration publique.

explain.written: The posted worker declaration (déclaration préalable de détachement) is an online notice that a foreign employer must submit to the French labour inspectorate before posting an employee to France, stating among other things the identity of the worker, the dates and the place of work.
explain.spoken: Before anyone's posted to France, the foreign employer has to file an online declaration with the labour inspectorate - and we, as the host, have to check it's been done.

def: An EU form showing which country's social security system covers a worker who works in more than one EU, EEA or Swiss state.

formal.ex: The posted worker shall be able to produce a [[portable document A1]] issued by the competent institution of the sending State.

everyday.ex: Without an [[A1 certificate]], the French authorities could ask us to pay contributions here as well.
everyday.ex_us: Without an [[A1 form]], the French authorities could ask us to pay contributions here as well.

informal.ex: Don't let him fly out until his [[A1]] has come through.

collocations: an A1 for a business trip
to remain covered by the home social security system
note_fr: Le formulaire A1 prouve que le salarié reste affilié au régime de son pays d'origine et dispense de cotisations dans l'État d'accueil. Il est exigé même pour des déplacements courts, et un contrôle sans A1 peut coûter cher. Il ne règle ni l'impôt, ni le droit du travail applicable.

fr: coordination des systèmes de sécurité sociale
def: The EU rules that decide which single country's social security system applies to a person who moves or works across borders.

formal.ex: Under the EU rules on the [[coordination of social security systems]], a worker is subject to the legislation of a single Member State at a time.

everyday.ex: It's a [[social security coordination]] question - she lives in Belgium but works three days a week in Lille.

note_fr: La coordination ne crée pas un régime européen : elle désigne quel régime national s'applique et évite la double affiliation. Le Royaume-Uni, depuis le Brexit, relève d'un accord spécifique avec l'UE : ne supposez pas que les anciennes règles s'appliquent telles quelles.

def: A document issued under a bilateral social security agreement confirming that a worker stays covered by the home country's system.

formal.ex: A [[certificate of coverage]] issued under the bilateral agreement exempts the assignee from host-country social security contributions for the period stated.

everyday.ex: Our US engineers need a [[coverage certificate]] before they start in Paris, otherwise we pay twice.

collocations: to request a certificate of coverage
note_fr: C'est l'équivalent hors Union européenne du formulaire A1, délivré en application d'une convention bilatérale. Les Américains disent « certificate of coverage » (US Social Security). Ne traduisez pas par « secondment certificate ».

def: A treaty between two countries that coordinates their social security systems for people who work in both.

formal.ex: The assignment falls within the scope of the [[bilateral social security agreement]] between France and India.
formal.ex_us: The assignment falls within the scope of the [[totalization agreement]] between the United States and France.

everyday.ex: Is there a [[social security agreement]] with Brazil, or will he have to contribute in both countries?
everyday.ex_us: Is there a [[totalization agreement]] with Brazil, or will he have to contribute in both countries?

collocations: to fall under a bilateral agreement
note_fr: Les Américains les appellent « totalization agreements », du nom du mécanisme de totalisation des périodes. Chaque convention a son propre champ et ses propres durées : ne généralisez jamais d'un pays à l'autre et vérifiez le texte applicable.

def: An optional French scheme that lets expatriates who leave the French system keep social security cover comparable to what they had at home.

formal.uk: voluntary affiliation to the French expatriate social security fund
formal.us: voluntary enrollment in the French expatriate social security fund
formal.ex: The Company shall bear the cost of the Assignee's [[voluntary affiliation to the French expatriate social security fund]].
formal.ex_us: The Company shall bear the cost of the Assignee's [[voluntary enrollment in the French expatriate social security fund]].

everyday.ex: She'll be on the local system in Singapore, but she wants [[to keep French-style cover]] through the CFE.
everyday.ex_us: She'll be on the local system in Singapore, but she wants [[to keep French-style coverage]] through the CFE.

note_fr: Un expatrié (au sens français) sort du régime français : la CFE lui permet de garder, s'il le souhaite, une couverture santé et accident du travail, et des solutions existent pour la retraite. « Cover » (UK) / « coverage » (US).

explain.written: The CFE (Caisse des Français de l'étranger) is a French voluntary social security fund that allows expatriates no longer covered by the French system to keep health and work-injury cover comparable to the French scheme.
explain.spoken: When someone leaves the French system to go abroad, they can join a voluntary fund called the CFE to keep French-style health cover - lots of companies pay for it.

def: Private medical insurance that covers an employee and family wherever they live, including treatment and emergency evacuation.

formal.ex: Assignees and accompanying family members shall be covered by the Group's [[international private medical insurance]].
formal.ex_us: Assignees and accompanying family members shall be covered by the Group's [[international medical plan]].

everyday.ex: Make sure her [[international health insurance]] is active from the day she lands.

collocations: to add dependants to the policy
note_fr: « Insurance » est indénombrable : « an insurance policy », pas « an insurance ». Vérifiez l'articulation avec la mutuelle et la prévoyance françaises : un expatrié peut perdre des garanties en quittant le régime collectif français.

fr: package aligné sur le pays d'origine
def: An assignment package that keeps the employee's home salary as the reference and adds allowances for the move.

formal.ex: Long-term assignees shall be remunerated under the [[home-based compensation approach]] described in Section 3.

everyday.ex: She's on a [[home-based package]], so her salary still follows the French pay review.

note_fr: Logique : le salarié reste « payé comme chez lui » et compte revenir. Utile pour les missions avec retour prévu. Le mot « package » s'emploie sans complexe en anglais pour l'ensemble rémunération et avantages.

fr: package aligné sur le pays d'accueil
def: An assignment package based on the pay levels of the host country, usually with some extra support.

formal.ex: Under the [[host-based compensation approach]], base salary shall be set by reference to the host-country salary structure.

everyday.ex: Putting him on a [[host-based package]] would cut his take-home pay quite a bit.

collocations: to be paid on local terms
note_fr: Le choix « home-based / host-based » a des effets d'équité dans l'équipe d'accueil : en France, des différences de rémunération entre salariés de même niveau doivent pouvoir se justifier par des éléments objectifs.

def: An extra payment, often a percentage of base salary, for accepting an assignment abroad.

formal.ex: A [[mobility premium]] equal to 10% of base salary shall be paid for the duration of the assignment.
formal.ex_us: A [[foreign service premium]] equal to 10% of base salary shall be paid for the duration of the assignment.

everyday.ex: Most companies have cut the [[expat premium]] - it used to be fifteen per cent.
everyday.ex_us: Most companies have cut the [[expat premium]] - it used to be fifteen percent.

note_fr: « Premium » = prime, supplément (et non « premier »). Faux ami : « prime » en anglais veut dire « de premier ordre » (« prime location »). « Per cent » (UK) / « percent » (US).

def: A policy under which the company pays the assignee's actual taxes and deducts what they would have paid had they stayed at home, so the assignment neither costs nor earns them tax.

formal.ex: The Assignee shall be subject to [[tax equalisation]] in accordance with the Group's tax equalisation policy.
formal.ex_us: The Assignee shall be subject to [[tax equalization]] in accordance with the Group's tax equalization policy.

everyday.ex: Don't worry about the higher tax rate here - you'll [[be tax-equalised]].
everyday.ex_us: Don't worry about the higher tax rate here - you'll [[be tax-equalized]].

note_fr: Orthographe UK en -isation, US en -ization. Prévenez le salarié : l'égalisation joue dans les deux sens, et s'il part dans un pays moins imposé, il ne garde pas l'économie d'impôt. Le règlement final (« tax equalisation settlement ») peut conduire le salarié à rembourser l'entreprise.

def: A policy under which the company pays only the extra tax an assignee owes because of the assignment, while the employee keeps any tax saving.

formal.ex: Short-term assignees shall benefit from [[tax protection]] whereby the Company bears any tax liability in excess of the hypothetical home-country tax.

everyday.ex: He's only [[tax-protected]], so if Dubai works out cheaper he keeps the difference.

note_fr: Différence avec l'égalisation : la protection ne joue que dans un sens (le salarié ne peut qu'y gagner). Ne promettez ni l'une ni l'autre par oral : elles reposent sur une politique écrite et des calculs de fiscalistes.

def: An agreement between two countries that decides which one may tax a given income, so that people are not taxed twice on it.

formal.ex: Under the applicable [[double tax treaty]], employment income is taxable in the State where the employment is exercised, subject to certain exceptions.
formal.ex_us: Under the applicable [[income tax treaty]], employment income is taxable in the State where the employment is exercised, subject to certain exceptions.

everyday.ex: Check the [[tax treaty]] - she might still be taxable in France on part of it.

note_fr: Une convention fiscale ne règle que l'impôt sur le revenu (et parfois d'autres impôts) : elle ne dit rien de la sécurité sociale, qui relève des règlements européens ou des conventions de sécurité sociale. Les deux se confondent souvent dans les e-mails du siège.

def: Moving an assignee onto local terms and a local contract in the host country, so that expatriate benefits end.

formal.ex: Upon [[localisation]], the Employee shall be employed by the host entity on local terms and conditions.
formal.ex_us: Upon [[localization]], the Employee shall be employed by the host entity on local terms and conditions.

everyday.ex: He's been here six years - it's time we [[localised]] him.
everyday.ex_us: He's been here six years - it's time we [[localized]] him.

informal.ex: She [[went local]] after her third year and bought a flat in Lyon.

note_fr: En RH, « localisation » n'a rien à voir avec la géolocalisation : c'est la fin du statut d'expatrié. Si le salarié quitte son contrat d'origine, traitez en droit français le sort de ce contrat (rupture, suspension, reprise d'ancienneté).

def: A local contract and salary with a few selected extra benefits, such as housing or schooling help, for a limited time.

formal.ex: Employees transferring at their own request may be offered a [[local-plus package]] for a maximum of two years.

everyday.ex: We can't offer full expat terms, but [[local plus]] with two years of school fees might do it.

note_fr: Formule de plus en plus fréquente pour les mobilités à l'initiative du salarié. Fixez par écrit la durée et la dégressivité des avantages (« tapering ») pour éviter qu'ils ne deviennent un usage.

def: In immigration law, a person who is not a citizen of the EU; in mobility, an assignee who is a national of neither the home nor the host country.

formal.ex: A [[third-country national]] may only take up employment in France if he or she holds a valid work authorisation.
formal.ex_us: A [[third-country national]] may only take up employment in France if he or she holds a valid work authorization.

everyday.ex: He's a [[TCN]] - Indian passport, employed in London, going to Paris - so check all three angles.

note_fr: Deux sens à distinguer : en droit européen de l'immigration, « third-country national » = ressortissant non-UE ; dans le jargon de la mobilité, c'est un salarié qui n'a la nationalité ni du pays d'origine ni du pays d'accueil. Demandez lequel est visé.

def: A French multi-year residence permit for certain highly skilled or qualified foreign nationals, which also covers their family.

formal.ex: The employee shall apply for a [[multi-year 'talent passport' residence permit]] in the category of highly qualified employee.

everyday.ex: With her salary and her master's, she should qualify for a [[talent passport]].

collocations: to qualify for a talent passport
note_fr: Pas d'équivalent exact au Royaume-Uni ou aux États-Unis : comparez-le, pour un interlocuteur étranger, à un titre de séjour pluriannuel pour profils qualifiés, sans avoir à démontrer l'absence de candidat local. Les critères (diplôme, salaire, catégorie) évoluent : vérifiez-les à chaque dossier.

explain.written: The talent passport (passeport talent) is a French multi-year residence permit for specific categories of highly skilled foreign nationals, such as highly qualified employees, which also allows accompanying family members to obtain a residence permit.
explain.spoken: The talent passport is a French permit for highly skilled people - it lasts several years and the family can come too, which makes it much easier than a standard work permit.

def: A residence and work permit for a manager, specialist or trainee from outside the EU who is temporarily transferred to a group company in the EU.

formal.ex: Managers and specialists seconded from the Indian entity may apply for an [[intra-corporate transferee permit]] for the duration of the transfer.
formal.ex_us: Managers and specialists seconded from the Indian entity may apply for an [[intracompany transferee permit]] for the duration of the transfer.

everyday.ex: The two architects from Pune can come over on an [[ICT permit]] - they've both been with the group long enough.

collocations: to be transferred within the group
note_fr: Ce dispositif européen vise les cadres, experts et stagiaires salariés d'un groupe établi hors UE qui restent liés à leur employeur d'origine. Il suppose une ancienneté minimale dans le groupe et une durée limitée. Aux États-Unis, le visa comparable est le L-1 : simple point de repère, les régimes diffèrent.

fr: titre de séjour pour la famille accompagnante
def: A visa or residence permit that allows the spouse or partner and children of a visa holder to live in the country.

formal.ex: The spouse shall apply for a [[dependant's residence permit]] at the same time as the main applicant.
formal.ex_us: The spouse shall apply for a [[dependent's residence permit]] at the same time as the main applicant.

everyday.ex: Can her husband work on a [[dependant visa]], or is it residence only?
everyday.ex_us: Can her husband work on a [[dependent visa]], or is it residence only?

collocations: the right to work for spouses
note_fr: Orthographe : en anglais britannique, le nom s'écrit « dependant » et l'adjectif « dependent » ; en américain, « dependent » dans les deux cas. La question cruciale pour le conjoint : peut-il travailler ? Posez-la tôt.

def: The time an authority takes to examine an application and reach a decision.

formal.ex: Applicants should allow for [[processing times]] of up to several weeks, which vary by consulate and by period.

everyday.ex: What's the [[lead time]] on a visa from Bangalore at the moment?

note_fr: « Instruction » est un faux ami : en anglais, c'est une consigne. Le délai d'instruction se dit « processing time ». Ne donnez jamais de date de démarrage ferme au siège avant d'avoir le titre en main : dites « subject to the visa coming through ».

def: A decision to make an assignment last longer than the period originally agreed.

formal.ex: Any [[extension of the assignment]] shall be agreed in writing at least three months before the scheduled end date.

everyday.ex: The business wants to [[extend her assignment]] by a year - can we do that without losing the A1?

collocations: to check the impact on tax and social security
note_fr: Une prolongation n'est jamais neutre : elle peut dépasser la durée maximale du détachement social, modifier la résidence fiscale ou exiger un nouveau titre de séjour. Faites une check-list avant de dire oui.

def: Ending an assignment before its planned end date, for business or personal reasons.

formal.ex: In the event of [[early termination of the assignment]] at the Assignee's initiative, the Company may recover part of the relocation costs.

everyday.ex: They had to [[cut the assignment short]] because her father fell ill.

note_fr: Distinguez bien la fin de la mission (le salarié rentre et retrouve un poste) et la fin du contrat de travail (licenciement, démission) : en anglais, « termination » seul évoque souvent la seconde. Écrivez « termination of the assignment ».

def: The group-wide framework that organises all jobs into families, levels and titles so they can be compared across countries.

formal.ex: All positions shall be mapped to the [[global job architecture]] no later than 31 December.
formal.ex_us: All positions shall be mapped to the [[global job architecture]] no later than December 31.

everyday.ex: The new [[job architecture]] has eight levels, and nobody in France knows where they sit yet.

collocations: to roll out a new architecture
note_fr: Une architecture des emplois groupe ne remplace pas la classification de la convention collective française : les deux coexistent et chaque salarié doit avoir un coefficient conventionnel. Prévoyez une table de correspondance.

fr: positionner un poste (dans la grille groupe)
def: To decide at which level of the group's job framework a position sits.

formal.uk: to determine the level of a position
formal.us: to determine the level of a position
formal.ex: Group Reward shall [[determine the level of a position]] on the basis of its scope and impact.

everyday.ex: Before we can post the job, Group need to [[level the role]].
everyday.ex_us: Before we can post the job, corporate needs to [[level the role]].

note_fr: « Levelled » (UK) / « leveled » (US). Ne confondez pas avec « to level up » (aligner par le haut) ni avec « level » au sens de niveau de langue. Le positionnement d'un poste ne change pas, à lui seul, la classification conventionnelle du salarié.

fr: addendum local (adaptation locale d'une politique groupe)
def: A document attached to a group policy that adapts or replaces some of its provisions to comply with local law.

formal.ex: Where required by local law, this Policy shall be supplemented by a [[country-specific addendum]], which shall prevail in case of conflict.

everyday.ex: We'll need a French [[local addendum]] - half of this policy won't work here as it stands.

note_fr: Pluriel : « addenda » ou, plus courant aujourd'hui, « addendums ». Présentez l'addendum au siège comme une condition de validité en France, pas comme une préférence : c'est plus convaincant que « in France we do things differently ».

def: The legal entity that holds the employment contract with a worker and has the legal obligations of an employer.

formal.ex: The French entity remains the [[legal employer]] and alone exercises disciplinary authority over the Employee.

everyday.ex: Whoever he reports to day to day, his [[actual employer]] is still the French company.

note_fr: Dans une organisation matricielle, le manager fonctionnel à l'étranger n'est pas l'employeur : en droit français, le pouvoir de direction et le pouvoir disciplinaire appartiennent à l'employeur juridique. Aux États-Unis, on entend aussi « employer of record » dans ce sens, mais l'expression désigne surtout le prestataire qui emploie pour le compte d'un client.

def: An external provider that organises and coordinates all the practical aspects of employees' international moves.

formal.ex: The [[relocation services provider]] shall act as single point of contact for the Assignee throughout the move.

everyday.ex: The [[relocation company]] will sort out the movers and temporary housing - you just sign off the quotes.

note_fr: « Vendor » (fournisseur) est très américain ; les Britanniques disent plus volontiers « supplier » ou « provider ». Tout prestataire qui traite des données des salariés doit être encadré contractuellement : pensez au RGPD.

def: Practical help on arrival in the host city, such as house-hunting, school search, registration and settling in.

formal.ex: The Company shall provide up to three days of [[destination services]], including home search and school search.

everyday.ex: They'll get two days of [[settling-in help]] - opening a bank account, the school visits, that sort of thing.

note_fr: « Destination services » est un terme du métier, peu parlant pour le salarié : à l'oral, dites « help finding a home and a school » ou « settling-in support ».

def: Training that prepares employees and families to live and work in another culture, or to work with colleagues from it.

formal.ex: Assignees and accompanying partners shall be offered one day of [[intercultural training]] before departure.

everyday.ex: Honestly, the US managers need [[cross-cultural training]] on France more than our people need it on the US.

note_fr: « Interculturel » se dit « cross-cultural » ou « intercultural » ; « multicultural » décrit une équipe ou une société composée de plusieurs cultures. Proposez la formation dans les deux sens : siège et filiale.

def: The hours of the working day that are shared by colleagues in different time zones.

formal.ex: Meetings involving several regions should, wherever possible, be held within [[core overlap hours]].

everyday.ex: We only get about two hours of [[overlap]] with the Chicago team, so let's not waste them on status updates.

note_fr: « Overlap » se prononce avec l'accent sur la première syllabe quand c'est un nom (/ˈəʊvəlæp/) et sur la dernière quand c'est un verbe (/ˌəʊvəˈlæp/). En France, rappelez que les réunions tardives restent soumises aux règles de durée du travail et au droit à la déconnexion.

def: To change the time of a recurring meeting so that each region takes turns having an inconvenient slot.

formal.ex: It is recommended [[to rotate meeting times]] so that the burden of early and late calls is shared fairly.

everyday.ex: Why don't we [[take turns]]? Europe takes the late slot one month, Asia the next.

note_fr: Prononciation : UK /rəʊˈteɪt/, US souvent /ˈroʊteɪt/. « To share the pain » est une expression idiomatique, bienveillante et très utilisée pour proposer cette rotation.

def: A way of collaborating in which people contribute at different times, through written updates and shared documents, rather than in live meetings.

formal.ex: Teams spread across more than two continents are encouraged to adopt [[asynchronous working]] practices.
formal.ex_us: Teams spread across more than two continents are encouraged to adopt [[asynchronous work]] practices.

everyday.ex: Can we do this one [[async]]? I'll drop my comments in the doc tonight.

note_fr: « Async » se prononce /ˈeɪsɪŋk/. Le travail asynchrone n'autorise pas à solliciter les salariés français à toute heure : le droit à la déconnexion s'applique quel que soit le fuseau horaire de l'émetteur.

def: An arrangement in which the employee works in another country during the week and returns home regularly, often at weekends.

formal.ex: Under a [[commuter assignment]], the employee's family remains in the home country and travel costs are borne by the Company.

everyday.ex: He [[commutes]] from Brussels to Paris every Monday and goes home on Thursday night.

note_fr: Les navetteurs posent des questions complexes de sécurité sociale (travail dans plusieurs États), de fiscalité et parfois de détachement : signalez-les tôt aux spécialistes. Ne confondez pas avec « frontalier » (« cross-border worker »), notion fiscale spécifique.

def: An employee who comes from abroad to work in the country of the company's head office or, more generally, in the country concerned.

formal.ex: An [[impatriate]] recruited from abroad may, subject to conditions, benefit from a specific tax regime in France.
formal.ex_us: An [[inpatriate]] recruited from abroad may, subject to conditions, benefit from a specific tax regime in France.

everyday.ex: We've got four [[inbound assignees]] this year and two going out.

note_fr: Le terme est surtout français : à l'étranger, on dit le plus souvent « inbound assignee » (salarié qui arrive) et « outbound assignee » (qui part). La forme américaine, quand elle est utilisée, est « inpatriate ».

fr: estimation du coût de la mission
def: A forecast of the total cost of an assignment, including salary, allowances, taxes and moving costs, prepared before approval.

formal.ex: No assignment shall be approved until an [[assignment cost estimate]] has been reviewed by the business sponsor.

everyday.ex: Once the business sees the [[cost projection]], they'll probably go for a local hire instead.

note_fr: Une mission coûte souvent bien plus que le salaire de base (impôts, logement, école, sécurité sociale) : présentez le coût complet (« fully loaded cost ») et non le seul brut, sinon le siège sera surpris.

fr: perdu à la traduction (malentendu culturel ou linguistique)
def: Describes a meaning or nuance that disappears when a message passes from one language or culture to another.

formal.ex: Some of the nuance of the French legal position may [[be lost in translation]]; a call may be preferable.

everyday.ex: I think the word 'mandatory' [[got lost in translation]] - in Paris they read it as 'recommended'.

note_fr: Expression très utile pour signaler un malentendu sans accuser personne. Pensez aussi à « to be at cross purposes » (parler de deux choses différentes sans s'en rendre compte).

def: Describes an approach applied identically everywhere without adapting it to local needs or laws.

formal.ex: A [[uniform approach]] across all jurisdictions is not achievable in the area of working time.

everyday.ex: A [[one-size-fits-all]] policy sounds efficient, but it'll hit a wall in France and Germany.

note_fr: Avec des traits d'union quand l'expression précède un nom (« a one-size-fits-all policy »). Une contre-proposition efficace face au siège : « global principles, local execution ».

def: Help given to the assignee's spouse or partner, such as language lessons, job-search assistance or an allowance.

formal.ex: The accompanying partner shall be eligible for the [[partner assistance programme]], including career counselling and language tuition.
formal.ex_us: The accompanying partner shall be eligible for the [[spouse/partner assistance program]], including career counseling and language tuition.

everyday.ex: She'll only say yes if there's some [[partner support]] - her husband doesn't want to give up his career.

note_fr: N'employez pas « spousal support » aux États-Unis : c'est la pension alimentaire après divorce. « Trailing spouse » (le conjoint qui suit) est courant mais jugé un peu dévalorisant ; préférez « accompanying partner ».

def: The process of bringing an assignee back into a role in the home organisation at the end of an assignment.

formal.ex: The home entity shall begin planning the Assignee's [[reintegration]] no later than six months before the end of the assignment.

everyday.ex: We always lose people at [[re-entry]] because there's no job waiting for them.
everyday.ex_us: We always lose people at [[reentry]] because there's no job waiting for them.

note_fr: UK « re-entry » avec trait d'union, US souvent « reentry ». Le retour est le point faible de beaucoup de mobilités : beaucoup de salariés partent dans les mois qui suivent leur retour s'ils n'ont pas de poste valorisant.

fr: être pris entre deux feux (double rattachement)

term.uk: to be caught in the middle
term.us: to be caught in the middle

def: To be in a difficult position between two people or sides who want different things, for example two managers.

formal.ex: An employee who [[receives conflicting instructions]] from the local and functional managers should refer the matter to HR.

everyday.uk: to be caught in the middle
everyday.us: to be caught in the middle
everyday.ex: She's [[caught in the middle]] - her Paris boss wants one thing and the global lead in Boston wants the opposite.

informal.uk: to be piggy in the middle
informal.us: to be stuck in the middle
informal.ex: I'm fed up [[being piggy in the middle]] between the two of them.
informal.ex_us: I'm tired of [[being stuck in the middle]] between the two of them.

note_fr: « Piggy in the middle » est britannique et familier (le jeu de la balle au prisonnier version deux contre un). Pour résoudre le conflit, revenez à l'employeur juridique et à une répartition écrite des rôles (« decision rights »).

fr: détachement de longue durée (au-delà de 12 mois)
def: Under EU rules, a posting that exceeds twelve months (or eighteen with a justified notification), after which almost all host-country employment rules apply.

formal.ex: Where the actual duration of a posting exceeds twelve months, the rules on [[long-term posting]] shall apply, unless a reasoned notification extending that period has been submitted.

everyday.ex: If he stays past the twelve-month mark, it becomes a [[long-term posting]] and pretty much the whole of French employment law kicks in.

note_fr: Au-delà de la durée-seuil, presque toutes les règles du pays d'accueil s'appliquent, à l'exception notamment des règles sur la conclusion et la rupture du contrat et des clauses de non-concurrence. Remplacer un détaché par un autre sur le même poste ne remet pas le compteur à zéro.

fr: noyau dur de règles du pays d'accueil (détachement)
def: The minimum set of host-country employment rules that must be applied to posted workers from the first day, such as minimum pay, working time and health and safety.

formal.uk: hard core of terms and conditions of employment
formal.us: hard core of terms and conditions of employment
formal.ex: The posting undertaking shall guarantee posted workers the [[hard core of terms and conditions of employment]] laid down in the host Member State.

everyday.ex: Even on a three-week posting, the [[core host-country rules]] apply - minimum pay, hours, rest, health and safety.

collocations: to compare home and host terms
note_fr: « Hard core » est l'expression du droit européen, mais en anglais courant « hardcore » a d'autres connotations : à l'oral, préférez « core rules » ou « the minimum French rules ». Le noyau dur comprend notamment la rémunération, la durée du travail et les repos, les congés payés et la santé-sécurité.

fr: représentant en France (de l'employeur étranger qui détache)
def: The person a foreign employer must appoint in France to liaise with the authorities for the duration of a posting.

formal.ex: The foreign employer shall appoint a [[representative in France]] to liaise with the labour inspectorate for the duration of the posting.

everyday.ex: Who's the [[designated representative]] for the Indian team - us, or someone from their side?

note_fr: Le représentant sert d'interlocuteur aux autorités françaises et doit pouvoir présenter les documents exigés, traduits en français. Ce n'est pas un mandataire général de l'entreprise étrangère : précisez son rôle par écrit.

def: The principle that periods of insurance completed in different countries are added together to open rights, especially to a pension.

formal.ex: Under the principle of [[aggregation of insurance periods]], periods completed in another Member State shall be taken into account where necessary to open entitlement.
formal.ex_us: Under the principle of [[aggregation of coverage periods]], periods completed in another country shall be taken into account where necessary to open entitlement.

everyday.ex: Her years in Germany will [[count towards]] her French pension rights, but each country pays its own share.
everyday.ex_us: Her years in Germany will [[count toward]] her French pension rights, but each country pays its own share.

collocations: a pension statement from each country
note_fr: La totalisation sert à ouvrir le droit ; ensuite, chaque pays verse en principe la part correspondant aux périodes accomplies chez lui. « Towards » (UK) / « toward » (US).

fr: approche du « bilan » (maintien du pouvoir d'achat d'origine)
def: A method of setting expatriate pay so that the assignee keeps the same purchasing power as at home, with allowances covering the differences in costs.

formal.ex: Expatriate remuneration shall be determined using the [[balance sheet approach]], with home-country net salary as the reference.

everyday.ex: We use the [[balance sheet]] for long-term moves, so she shouldn't be better or worse off.

collocations: to be no better and no worse off
note_fr: Rien à voir avec le bilan comptable, malgré le nom. L'idée à retenir : « no better, no worse off ». Méthode coûteuse, en recul dans beaucoup de groupes au profit de formules plus proches du marché local.

def: The amount deducted from a tax-equalised assignee's pay, equal to the tax they would have paid had they stayed at home.

formal.ex: A [[hypothetical tax]] shall be withheld from the Assignee's salary and reconciled after the end of each tax year.

everyday.ex: The [[hypo tax]] comes off her payslip every month, and the company pays the real tax in both countries.
everyday.ex_us: The [[hypo tax]] comes off her pay stub every month, and the company pays the real tax in both countries.

note_fr: « Hypo tax » est le raccourci universel chez les spécialistes. Expliquez au salarié que cette retenue n'est pas un impôt versé à l'État mais une retenue interne qui finance l'égalisation fiscale.

def: An arrangement in which an employee's pay is delivered partly through the home payroll and partly through the host payroll.

formal.ex: Under the [[split payroll arrangement]], 60% of base salary shall be paid in France and the balance in the United States.

everyday.ex: He's on a [[split payroll]] - part in euros here, part in dollars into his US account.

collocations: to be paid in two currencies
note_fr: La paie éclatée concerne la façon de verser le salaire ; elle ne règle pas, à elle seule, la question de l'impôt ou des cotisations. Chaque fraction peut avoir ses propres obligations déclaratives.

def: A payroll run in the host country only to report and withhold tax or contributions, while the salary itself is still paid in the home country.

formal.ex: The host entity shall operate a [[shadow payroll]] in order to comply with local reporting and withholding obligations.

everyday.uk: to put someone on shadow payroll
everyday.us: to put someone on shadow payroll
everyday.ex: He's still paid from Mumbai, but we'll need [[to put him on shadow payroll]] here for the tax side.

note_fr: « Shadow » ne veut pas dire « au noir » : la paie fictive est au contraire un outil de conformité. Avec le prélèvement à la source en France, la question se pose dès qu'un salarié payé à l'étranger devient imposable en France.

def: Increasing a payment so that, after tax and contributions, the employee receives the intended net amount.

formal.ex: Relocation expenses shall be subject to a [[tax gross-up]] so that the Assignee bears no tax on such benefits.

everyday.ex: If we want her to get the full ten thousand, we'll have [[to gross it up]].

note_fr: Nom avec trait d'union (« a gross-up »), verbe sans (« to gross up »). Un brutage coûte souvent bien plus que prévu, car l'impôt sur l'impôt est lui-même imposable : faites chiffrer avant de promettre un net.

def: A French tax scheme under which people who move to France for work after living abroad may be partly exempted from income tax for a limited number of years.

formal.ex: The employee may be eligible for the [[special tax regime for impatriates]], subject to meeting the statutory conditions.
formal.ex_us: The employee may be eligible for the [[special tax regime for inpatriates]], subject to meeting the statutory conditions.

everyday.ex: Have we checked whether she qualifies for the [[impat regime]]? It makes a real difference to her net.
everyday.ex_us: Have we checked whether she qualifies for the [[inpat regime]]? It makes a real difference to her net.

collocations: for a limited number of years
note_fr: Ne détaillez pas les conditions de mémoire : elles portent notamment sur la résidence fiscale antérieure et la durée, et elles évoluent. Renvoyez au conseiller fiscal. Le Royaume-Uni et les États-Unis n'ont pas d'équivalent direct.

explain.written: The French impatriate tax regime (régime des impatriés) allows employees who take up a post in France after a period of tax residence abroad to benefit, under strict conditions and for a limited number of years, from a partial income tax exemption on certain elements of their remuneration.
explain.spoken: France has a special tax scheme for people coming in from abroad - for a few years, part of their pay can be tax-free, as long as they meet the conditions.

def: The risk that an employee's activity in a country creates a taxable presence there for the company.

formal.ex: Remote working from abroad shall not be approved where it gives rise to a [[permanent establishment risk]] for the Company.

everyday.ex: If he's signing contracts from Madrid, that's a [[PE risk]] - tax won't sign off on it.

note_fr: C'est un risque pour l'entreprise (impôt sur les sociétés), distinct de l'impôt personnel du salarié. Il est particulièrement sensible pour les commerciaux ou dirigeants qui négocient ou signent depuis l'étranger. « Establishment » ici n'a rien à voir avec l'établissement distinct du droit du travail.

fr: employeur de référence (prestataire qui emploie pour le compte du client)
def: A third-party provider that legally employs a worker in a country on behalf of a company that has no entity there.

formal.ex: Where the Group has no legal entity in the country concerned, the employee may be engaged through an [[employer of record]].

everyday.ex: We don't have an entity in Portugal, so we'd have to hire her through an [[EOR]].

note_fr: Pratique très répandue dans les groupes américains. En France, ce montage doit être analysé au regard des règles sur le prêt de main-d'œuvre et le portage salarial, qui l'encadrent strictement : faites-le valider avant de l'accepter.

def: A role in which an employee works for a team or entity in another country without moving there, travelling only occasionally.

formal.ex: Where physical relocation is not required, the role may be performed as a [[virtual assignment]] from the home country.

everyday.ex: Instead of moving him to Boston, couldn't he [[do the role remotely]] and fly over once a quarter?

note_fr: Solution moins coûteuse qu'une expatriation, mais pas sans risques : voyages fréquents, risque d'établissement stable, question du manager et de l'employeur juridique. Vérifiez qui fixe les objectifs et qui évalue.

def: Rules of a country's law that must be applied to a situation whatever law the parties have chosen, because they protect essential public interests.

formal.ex: The choice of law shall not prevent the application of the [[overriding mandatory provisions]] of the law of the place where the work is carried out.

everyday.uk: rules you can't contract out of
everyday.us: rules you can't contract out of
everyday.ex: Choosing English law won't help: these are [[rules you can't contract out of]] in France.

collocations: the law chosen by the parties
note_fr: En droit européen, le choix de la loi applicable au contrat de travail ne peut pas priver le salarié de la protection des règles impératives de la loi qui s'appliquerait sans ce choix, et certaines lois de police s'imposent en tout état de cause. « Mandatory » = impératif, pas « mandaté ».

def: A culture in which much of the meaning is conveyed implicitly, through relationships, tone and context, rather than in explicit words.

formal.ex: In a [[high-context culture]], a refusal may be expressed indirectly and should not be read as agreement.

everyday.ex: When the Bangalore team say 'we'll try', you have to [[read between the lines]] - it often means 'no'.

note_fr: Notion de l'anthropologue Edward T. Hall, souvent citée en formation interculturelle. Gardez la nuance : ce sont des tendances, pas des règles. « To spell things out » (tout expliciter) est l'attitude attendue dans une culture à contexte pauvre.

fr: protection contre le risque de change
def: A mechanism that adjusts an assignee's pay or allowances when currency movements reduce their value beyond an agreed threshold.

formal.ex: A [[currency protection mechanism]] shall apply where the exchange rate varies by more than 5% over a six-month period.

everyday.ex: There's no [[currency protection]] in her package, so the fall in the rupee hit her savings.

collocations: to be paid in two currencies
note_fr: « Currency » = monnaie, devise ; « exchange » seul ne suffit pas. Précisez dans la lettre de mission le seuil, la période de référence et la source du taux.

fr: échec de mission (retour prématuré ou mission non réussie)
def: An assignment that ends early or does not meet its objectives, often because of family or adaptation problems.

formal.ex: The main causes of [[assignment failure]] are family difficulties and poor preparation before departure.

everyday.ex: It just [[didn't work out]] - his wife was miserable and they came back after eight months.

collocations: the cost of a failed assignment
note_fr: Évitez de qualifier publiquement un salarié de « failure » : parlez de l'affectation (« the assignment didn't work out »), pas de la personne. La préparation de la famille est le premier facteur de réussite.

def: An arrangement in which the employee works a set period in a remote location, then has a set period of rest at home, in a repeating cycle.

formal.ex: Employees on a [[rotational assignment]] shall work four weeks on site followed by two weeks' rest in the home country.

everyday.ex: He's [[on rotation]] - a month on the platform, then a month at home.

informal.ex: It's [[four on, two off]], so he's actually home quite a lot.

note_fr: Courant dans l'énergie, les mines et les grands chantiers. Les règles françaises de durée du travail et de repos restent à vérifier lorsque le contrat est français : le cycle « on/off » doit s'articuler avec elles.

fr: obligation de rapatriement et de reclassement (par la société mère)
def: Under French law, the duty of a French parent company to bring back and offer a new job to an employee it placed with a foreign subsidiary who is dismissed by that subsidiary.

formal.uk: statutory obligation to repatriate and redeploy
formal.us: statutory obligation to repatriate and redeploy
formal.ex: Should the subsidiary dismiss the Employee, the parent company shall be bound by its [[statutory obligation to repatriate and redeploy]] the Employee.

everyday.uk: to have to bring someone back
everyday.us: to have to bring someone back
everyday.ex: If the US subsidiary lets her go, we'll [[have to bring her back]] and find her a job here.

collocations: to redeploy within the parent company
note_fr: Règle française méconnue des sièges étrangers : lorsqu'un salarié engagé par une société mère française est mis à disposition d'une filiale étrangère qui le licencie, la société mère doit assurer son rapatriement et lui proposer un nouvel emploi compatible avec ses fonctions antérieures.

explain.written: Under French law, where an employee hired by a French parent company has been placed with a foreign subsidiary and is dismissed by that subsidiary, the parent company must arrange the employee's repatriation and offer a new position compatible with the duties previously held within it.
explain.spoken: In France, if we send someone to a foreign subsidiary and they're let go out there, we have to bring them home and offer them a suitable job here - we can't just walk away.

fr: correspondance entre grades groupe et classification conventionnelle
def: The exercise of matching each local job or classification level to a level in the group's global grading structure.

formal.ex: A [[grade mapping]] table shall be maintained to show the correspondence between global grades and the classification levels of the applicable collective agreement.

everyday.ex: We've [[mapped]] the French coefficients to the global grades, but a few roles don't fit anywhere.

collocations: to map local roles to global grades
note_fr: « To map to » = faire correspondre. Rappelez au siège que le grade global n'a pas de valeur juridique en France : c'est la classification conventionnelle qui détermine notamment le salaire minimum applicable.

fr: organisation « follow the sun » (relais entre fuseaux horaires)
def: Describes a way of organising work so that teams in successive time zones hand tasks on to each other and work continues around the clock.

formal.ex: Payroll support is delivered under a [[follow-the-sun model]] shared between the Manila, Kraków and Mexico City centres.

everyday.ex: With [[follow-the-sun]] support, Paris hands over to Mexico at six and picks it back up from Manila in the morning.

note_fr: Avec traits d'union devant un nom (« a follow-the-sun model »). « To hand over to » = passer le relais. L'organisation ne doit pas conduire à faire travailler les équipes françaises hors de leurs horaires.

def: The degree to which people in a culture accept that power and authority are distributed unequally.

formal.ex: Cultures with high [[power distance]] tend to expect decisions to be taken at the top and communicated downwards.

everyday.ex: Head office isn't remotely [[hierarchical]] - the VP will expect you to call her Sarah and to challenge her.

note_fr: Concept issu des travaux de Geert Hofstede, très utilisé en formation interculturelle. Utile pour expliquer pourquoi un siège américain ou néerlandais attend qu'on le contredise ouvertement, alors que d'autres cultures l'éviteront.

ipa.uk: /ˌwʌn ˈhʌndrəd ənd ˌeɪti ˈθriː deɪ ˌruːl/

def: A common tax treaty rule under which pay for short periods of work in another country is taxed only in the home country if certain conditions are met, including a stay of no more than 183 days.

formal.ex: The Assignee's remuneration may remain taxable in the home State only if the conditions of the [[183-day rule]] laid down in the applicable treaty are met.

everyday.ex: As long as he [[stays under 183 days]] and France isn't bearing the cost, he should stay taxable in the UK.

collocations: the cost recharged to the host entity
note_fr: Erreur classique : croire qu'en dessous de 183 jours on n'est jamais imposable à l'étranger. La règle conventionnelle comporte plusieurs conditions cumulatives (notamment que la rémunération ne soit pas supportée par une entité du pays d'accueil), et la période de référence varie selon les conventions. Les Américains disent « one hundred eighty-three », sans « and ».

def: An approved departure from the standard terms of a policy for a specific case.

formal.ex: Any [[exception to policy]] shall be approved in writing by the Global Mobility Director and documented in the assignment file.

everyday.ex: Can we push for an [[exception]]? Her son's in his final year of school, so the timing's terrible.

note_fr: « Dérogation » ne se traduit pas par « derogation » dans ce sens : en anglais, le mot est rare et juridique (dérogation à un traité). Dites « exception ». Rappelez le risque de précédent : « we don't want to set a precedent ».

def: The difficulty some employees and families have readjusting to their home country after living abroad.

formal.ex: Returning assignees may experience [[reverse culture shock]], which the re-entry programme seeks to address.

everyday.uk: to struggle to settle back in
everyday.us: to struggle to settle back in
everyday.ex: After four years in Singapore, they [[struggled to settle back in]] - Paris felt small and grey.

note_fr: Souvent sous-estimé, y compris par le salarié lui-même. « To settle back in » = se réadapter, se réinstaller ; à distinguer de « to settle in » (s'installer, à l'arrivée).
